original_question: Let M be a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J), and let its Sasaki cone be the cone of rays of Sasaki metrics compatible with that structure. Suppose the cone contains an extremal ray, meaning a ray represented by a Sasaki metric whose scalar curvature has transversely holomorphic gradient; constant scalar curvature Sasaki metrics are a special case of extremal metrics. Does it follow that the same Sasaki cone must contain at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 2 (the exact matching statement in the arXiv version): "If there are extremal rays of Sasaki metrics in the Sasaki cone, is there always at least one constant scalar curvature ray?"
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right open problem, the correct fixed-background setting of a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J), the existential implication from an extremal ray to a constant-scalar-curvature Sasaki ray, and the fact that constant scalar curvature Sasaki metrics are a special case of extremal metrics. Your description of extremality via transversely holomorphic gradient is also consistent with the paper's review of the definition.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is labeled Problem 2 in the Introduction; it is posed as an open problem, not as a theorem or conjecture with a proof.

The paper distinguishes the unreduced Sasaki cone t^+(D, J), the reduced cone kappa(D, J) = t^+(D, J)/W, and the space of rays R(D, J); the phrase "the Sasaki cone be the cone of rays" conflates these objects.

A ray means a transverse-scaling class r_xi of compatible Sasakian structures/Reeb vector fields; the paper explicitly notes that extremal and cscS structures come in rays because these properties are preserved under transverse scaling.
The fixed geometric data are a compact connected manifold M^{2n+1} and a contact CR structure (D, J) of Sasaki type.
In the paper, extremality is introduced variationally via the Calabi functional on S(xi, J-bar), and Lemma 3.4 gives equivalent formulations: s_g^T lies in H_xi, or equivalently pi_g(s_g^T) = s_g^T.
The paper's terminology is "constant scalar curvature Sasaki" (cscS); in this context this is the special extremal case emphasized in Section 2.2.
The nearby context also gives an explicit equivalent K-stability reformulation relative to a fixed maximal torus T, which your draft does not mention.
refined_question: Let M^{2n+1} be a compact connected manifold with a fixed contact CR structure (D, J) of Sasaki type. Let t^+(D, J) be the unreduced Sasaki cone of compatible Reeb vector fields, let R(D, J) be its set of rays under transverse scaling (equivalently, one may work in the reduced cone kappa(D, J) = t^+(D, J)/W), and suppose R(D, J) contains an extremal Sasaki ray r_xi, i.e. a ray represented by a compatible Sasakian structure S = (xi, eta, Phi, g) whose scalar curvature has transversely holomorphic (1,0)-gradient, equivalently whose transverse scalar curvature satisfies s_g^T in H_xi or pi_g(s_g^T) = s_g^T. Must the same Sasaki cone also contain at least one constant scalar curvature Sasaki ray (a cscS ray)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the paper's K-stability language: if a Sasaki cone admits a K-semistable polarization relative to a fixed maximal torus T, must it also admit a K-semistable polarization with respect to an arbitrary torus?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's exact intent: it is essentially Section 1, Problem 2 verbatim. The main refinements needed for a stand-alone, paper-faithful formulation are notational and contextual: the paper fixes a compact connected Sasaki manifold with contact CR structure (D, J), distinguishes t^+(D, J), its ray space R(D, J), and the reduced cone kappa(D, J), and reviews extremality both variationally and through the equivalent conditions in Lemma 3.4. I therefore kept the question narrow and did not broaden it to the neighboring Problem 1 about isolation of cscS rays or to special join constructions where partial affirmative results are known.
